Commentary.Commentary: Short ball was the key to keep this innings short. None of the batsmen could adjust to the short stuff and were found wanting. Windies were excellent and would want to wrap it up quickly. Around an hour to play before the Supper break.

Unbelievable. Who would have thought this? Winning the toss and electing to field and dismantling the opposition inside 30 overs. Bairstow departed cheaply and then England managed to get some partnerships going but none substantial.

OUT! BOWLED! Lock, stock and barrell! Yorker, at the base of the stumps, Curran backs a long away, exposes all his stumps and Thomas hits them. Perfect strike. 5-fer for Thomas, his first in ODIs. WINDIES NEED 114 TO WIN!
Mark Wood is the last man in.
OUT! Caught behind! Holder has his second. A short ball, outside off, Rashid looks to defend but the ball keeps on climbing and takes the outside edge behind. Simple catch to Hope.
The batsman has been hit on the glove or forearm.
Down the leg side, Rashid misses his tuck and the ball goes off his waist to the keeper behind. There is an appeal but it is silenced.
Outside off, left alone.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Around off, defended from the crease.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Tom Curran is in.

OUT! Buttler falls too! Probably the final nail in the coffin. England are failing miserably. A short ball, around middle and off, Buttler looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball swirls in the air and Sheldon Cottrell takes it calmly at deep square leg.
Down the leg side, helped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Adil Rashid walks in at number 9, replacing Woakes.
OUT! Top edge and taken! Number 7 falls. A short ball, around middle, Woakes looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball goes nowhere and Carlos Brathwaite takes it calmly at short mid-wicket.
On a good length around middle, defended watchfully.
Landed outside off, played straight to point.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Around off, defended watchfully.
A short ball, pulled to mid-wicket.
Outside off, let through again.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A short ball outside off, swayed away from.
Jason Holder into the attack. 5-0-28-1 so far.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Woakes comes in.
OUT! Caught behind! Short ball again, wicket once more. Short and outside off, Moeen looks to cut but the extra bounce consumes him. Takes a thick outside edge which is taken calmly by the keeper.
The batsman goes for the pull but misses it completely.
Outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Full and outside off, Moeen looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge to third man. A run taken.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side.
FOUR! Full and around off, slogged over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
TOP EDGE, SAFE! Short and around middle, Moeen looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball however, does not carry to fine leg. A single taken.
Outside off, punched through point for a couple.
Around off and middle watchfully defended.
A short ball, around off, Moeen hops to play that down.
A length ball down the leg side, Moeen misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Pretty straight, no turn, arrowed down the leg side, defended towards short mid-wicket.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Much fuller, in line of the stumps, clipped through mid-wicket for a run.
Dropped short, pulled through backward square leg for a couple.
WIDE. Down the leg side, left alone.

Full and outside off, Buttler drives it through mid off where Jason Holder dives but lands awkwardly on the ground. Holds his shoulder in pain. The ball goes to long off and a couple of runs are taken.
A length ball down the leg side, Moeen looks to tuck it to the leg side but misses and is hit on the thigh pads.
A short ball, around middle and leg, Moeen hops and works it in front of short leg.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Around middle and leg, flicked to the leg side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a run.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Down the leg side, helped through mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. One run added to the total.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Moeen Ali walks in at number 7, replacing Stokes.

OUT! Caught down the leg side! Another wicket of a short ball. Another partnership broken after a start. A short ball, down the leg side, Stokes looks to pull but the extra bounce does him in. Takes the top edge and Hope takes it easily. England in big trouble.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.
On a good length around off, Buttler looks to defend but gets a bit of an outside edge.
Now brings the sweep out and hits it towards deep square leg for a run. AN expensive first from Nurse. 9 from it.
FOUR! That is right in the slot there. Tossed up ball outside off, Buttler leans into it and strokes it through extra cover. No stopping that.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.

Short and outside off, Stokes slaps it through covers. They take one and then go for the second. Hetmyer there makes good ground to his left in the deep and then fires a throw to the bowler. He collects it and dislodges the stumps but the batsman is in.
The inside edge probably saves him there. The arm ball on off, Stokes looks to defend outside the line but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
On the shorter side, Buttler works it through mid-wicket and takes a single.
Ashley Nurse is now into the attack. Spinner for the first time today.
Shuffles right across and works it towards wide mid on for a single.
Angles this one into the batsman, Buttler blocks it off the front foot.
Comes down the track again and gets a short ball on the body, Stokes works it towards the leg side for a quick run.
Stokes uses his feet but Brathwaite outsmarts him with a short ball outside off. Ben leaves it alone.
Similar length, no movement this time, Stokes guides it to point.

JAFFA! Lands it on a length around off which means the batsman has to play at it. The ball though straightens and just about kisses the outside edge. Not a lot you can do with those but expect that it misses the outside edge.
Short again, this is on the body, Stokes pulls it towards fine leg for an easy single. Good over this for the visitors, 9 from it.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Hammered! That made a cracking sound off the bat! Short and on off, Stokes gets into position quickly and pulls it powerfully through mid-wicket for the second boundary of the over.
Better! Closer to the off pole and on a length. Buttler guides it to the slip fielder!
FOUR! Poor bowling! Short and wide outside off, Buttler slaps it through covers and a boundary results.
Back of a length on off, the batter stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Well fielded! Full and outside off, Buttler goes for the drive but the ball flies off the outside edge past the two slip fielders. Third man does well to run to his left and save a couple.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Third leave in a row as once again it is bowled outside off.
Outside off again, another leave.
Beaten all ends up! Brathwaite lands it on a length around off, Buttler walks ahead and looks to flick but the ball pitches and moves away. Beating the outside edge of Buttler's bat.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Short and wide outside off, let through.
WIDE. Short and well over the head of Stokes, left alone and wided.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman does well to leave that bouncer.
Man Of The Moment, Jos Buttler, is at the crease.

OUT! The short ball ploy works and captain Morgan is out of here! Morgan looks to play the pull but the extra bounce does him in. The angle cramps him too, with Thomas coming in from around the wicket. A top edge is induced and Sheldon Cottrell at fine leg, going back a few paces, takes it comfortably. 63/4 then... This may not be a 300 pitch. 230-240 could be a winning total.
FOUR! Just too wide outside off, on a length, Morgan just punches it through point.
Outside off, left alone.
Goes back in his crease and blocks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around middle, Ben looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Comes down the track to counter the swing but can only defend.
Massive movement. Terrific bowling. Lands it in the tempting area, inviting Stokes to drive, the all-rounder obliges but then the ball pitches and moves away to beat the outside edge.
Full and outside off, Stokes comes forward to defend but the ball swings away past the outside edge.
The batsman has stood up on his toes to play that one. End of a fiery over.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Full and outside off, Morgan leans and drives uppishly but it does not carry to short extra cover.
Short and outside off, Morgan slashes but misses.
A short ball, around middle and leg, Stokes takes his hands off that one. The ball hits the handle of the bat and goes towards square leg. A single taken.
Cut into half. On a good length around middle, Stokes looks to push but the ball comes back in and beats the inside edge. Yes, inside.
Oshane Thomas into the attack.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Down the leg side, Stokes misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads. Hope dives to his right and stops the ball.
Outside off, left alone.

OUT! Caught behind! There is that extra bounce and Hales departs. Short and outside off, Alex looks to cut but is cramped for room due to the extra bounce and gets an outside edge. Simple catch for Shai Hope. The partnership was just beginning to brew, worth 39... Ben Stokes walks in now.
Short and outside off, cut behind point for a couple.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
FOUR! Another lovely shot. Full and outside off, Morgan leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary!
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
On a good length around middle, watchfully defended.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.

DROPPED, FOUR! Shimron Hetmyer it is. Struggled during the Tests, has put one down again. Short and wide outside off, Hales smashes it through point. Hetmyer dives to his right from backward point and should have taken it, really. The ball hits his right palm and bursts through.
Short and wide outside off, Hales slashes but misses.
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Short and wide outside off, Eoin slashes hard but misses.
Outside off, left alone.
Half volley outside off, Morgan leans and drives it through the covers for a couple.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Landed outside off, let through again.
Full and outside off, Hales shoulders arms.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Smashes the bones out of this one. Up and over point.
FOUR! The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. The ball has crossed the ropes. The umpire signals four runs.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! In the air but in the gap! Full and outside off, Morgan leans and drives. The ball is in the air exactly between cover and point. Races to the fence.
Full and around middle, Hales gets across and works it in front of square on the leg side for a run.
FOUR! Nice drive. Full and around middle, Holder drives it down the ground and calls for a quick single. Mid on dives to his left but misses. Forget the single. Save your legs.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, Morgan looks to drive but gets an outside edge towards third man. A single taken.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, flick shot missed.
Nothing on the Free Hit. A length ball, outside off, Hales swings but misses.
FREE HIT TIME.

NO BALL! Oops... that has slipped out of the hands. Cottrell slips and so does the ball, out of his hand. Goes way outside the pitch and lands near Ashley Nurse at second slip! Anyone remembering Steve Harmison? Ashes 2006?
Full and around off, driven down the ground. Mid off makes a good diving save to his right.
WIDE. Appeal for a caught behind down the leg side, bu wide signalled. Hales missed his flick and some of the players appealed but no review taken.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
Outside off, left alone.
Landed around middle and leg, cutting back in, worked towards mid-wicket.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Landed outside off, moving away, Morgan feels for it but misses.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Outside off, steered to third man for a single.
Captain Eoin Morgan walks in at number 4, replacing Root.

OUT! Catching practice and full marks to Joe Root! This is poor batting and all of a sudden, Windies have two in the bag. A short ball, outside off, Root gets on top of the bounce and plays the upper cut. Very nice shot, when one first sees it. The ball flies in the air but oops... Sheldon Cottrell is waiting for it at squarish third man! Did Root not see that man over there? Or did he intend to play it finer? Well, he can contemplate that in the dressing room. Holder is pumped up!
Around middle and leg, watchfully defended back to the bowler. A stare from Cottrell to the batsman.
WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
An edge now. Full and wide outside off, Root looks to drive but the ball swings away, takes the outside edge and flies down to third man. A streaky single to get off the mark.
Joe Root walks in at number 3, replacing Bairstow.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! The leg stump has gone for a walk. Full and outside off, Bairstow looks to drive but does not look to move his feet. There is a big gap between bat and pad and the ball cannons off the inside edge onto the stumps. Replays show that there was a hint of inswing as well. Early break for the military man.
TOP EDGE, FOUR! Decent ball from Cottrell. Short ball, aimed at the body, Bairstow looks to pull but is cramped for room. Gets a top edge which flies over the keeper to the fine leg fence.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, left alone this time.

What a peach. After a string of loose balls, suddenly Holder slips in a lovely ball. Pitches this on a good length, just outside off, Hales looks to play but then the ball nibbles past the outside edge.
Full and around middle, finally a legal ball, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
HAT-TRICK OF WIDES NOW. Almost like playing the same tape again and again. One more down the leg side.
ANOTHER WIDE. Again, struggling with the breeze and line, slips this down the leg side, does Jason.
WIDE. Short and down the leg side, Bairstow lets it go.
Hales is off the mark. Flicks this off his pads to get to the other end.
Short ball outside off, Hales looks to cut it but fails to connect.
On the hips of the batsman who tucks it away around the corner for a single.
Jason Holder to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
On the pads, Bairstow turns it away to the on side to retain strike for the next one. England are 6/0 after the first over.
Length on the leg side again. Bairstow tries working this away but misses. The ball hits his thigh pad.
Around off, Bairstow plays it with a straight bat towards mid on.
WIDE! Goes full on the pads, Bairstow covers his stumps and let's it go. Wide given.
Back of a length again on top of off. Jonny jumps to keep it out.
Sheldon Cottrell seems to be having trouble near the landing area. He has requested for some sawdust to be applied in that region.
FOUR! First runs of the day. Similar line and length. This time Bairstow hops and and gets it fine to the fine leg boundary.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands this on a back of a length of the leg side. Bairstow looks to nudge it but gets it on the thigh pad.
Time to get going. The players are on the field. Alex Hales and Jonny Bairstow are the openers for England. Sheldon Cottrell will run up with the first ball.
TEAM NEWS - Windies are unchanged while the visitors have a solitary one. Liam Plunkett has an injury and is replaced by Tom Curran in this all-important final game.
TOSS - Windies have won the toss and elect to field first.

Welcome to game number 5 and the final match of this ODI series. Huge sixes and big scores have been the flavor of this rubber between the Windies and England so far. Heading into the final game, the hosts are trailing 1-2 with one game being washed out. They will hope to win this one and tie the series. St.Lucia is the third venue for the ODIs and the factor of the unknown will be there for both sides. As has been the series' pattern so far, the team who manages to bowl better should end up on the winning side. All eyes on the bowling units hence. Can Caribbean calypso beat this English batting machine that is smashing the smithereens out of bowling attacks? Or will the away side take home the trophy? All to play for, toss to follow...
